name: Lantern Valley
world: a narrow green valley at dusk, lit by hand: paper lanterns hung along the paths and floating on the river, a single-arch stone footbridge, pollarded willows leaning over the water, a stone lantern house at the inlet, and snow-capped mountains closing the far end
palette: deep dusk blues and violets in the sky, warm amber and honey-gold lantern light pooling on everything it touches, dark green conifers, pale stone
light: always near dusk or after dark. The light sources are lanterns and a low sun, never overhead daylight. Shadows are long and soft; lantern glow is the warmest thing in every frame
recurring: paper lanterns, round and ribbed, with a candle inside
Lumi's star-shaped lantern on a brass frame
the single-arch stone footbridge over the river
the stone lantern house at the water's inlet
willows and reeds at the water's edge
forbidden: electric or modern lighting of any kind
bright midday sun or flat overhead daylight
a wide lake or open sea; this is a river in a narrow valley
deciduous autumn woodland, which belongs to The Crooked Root
notes: Written after three books were generated independently and only the
CHARACTERS were held consistent. Palette, light and environment were
re-invented per book, so the valley drifted: one book's river is a broad
bright lake, another's is a frozen stream at sunset. A series a child
returns to has to be the same place each time -- that is most of what
makes it a place at all.
This is injected into every page prompt of every book in the series, the
same way a character bible is. See seriesWorld() in compile-prompt.mjs.
